about: Round 4's routing table, pre-registered data. Decided by routing.py only, from harness-side records only, never from the agent's text. Route, phase, turn-end and batch-state strings are graders/labels4.py's and are checked against it on load. A row matches when the take is in its phase, every all_of condition holds, at least one any_of condition holds (when any_of is given), and no none_of condition holds. The winning rows are the matched rows at the highest precedence level; matched rows at that level that name different routes are a tie and are refused, as is an input that matches no row. Rows never read a text-derived count (the events record): those are annotations, below.
plan_source: Round 4 plan, 'What round 4 measures' > 'Outcomes' > routing table and its precedence paragraph; CP1 task 'CREATE .../routing.py'.
precedence_source: Plan: 'pause, then aborted, then harness-error, then graded'. Lane w1b decision: rehearsal shares harness-error's level (both are harness faults, split only by phase), so a double match between them is refused, never picked.

rate_limit_markers.source: glitch-f3's ruling (in-plan, 6 Oct 2026, on lane w1b's open question whether a subscription usage-limit refusal carries a structured field; recorded as glitch-f3's, not the owner's): "Keep both: structured (status 429, type rate_limit_error) OR round 3's four text markers ('rate limit', 'usage limit', 'weekly limit', '429'), word-bounded and case-insensitive, matched on the harness-side error text only, never on the agent's own output. Make the small schema change so the API-error record carries that text." status and type match by exact membership. text is the API-error record's harness-side error text (what Claude Code or the API reported as the error, never the agent's reply), and it matches when it carries a text marker by round 3's bounded search (routing.rate_limit_text_marker): each marker word-bounded and case-insensitive. Round 3's origin: the text markers are round 3's RATE_LIMIT_MARKERS, in order, from evals/gap-study-3/drive.py:149 at e2979b3143081824aadea73523ec41af30c1ddb1 (which that line names as prereg.json driver_constants.rate_limit_markers; prereg.json itself was not read by lane w1b for this), matched there by matched_marker and looks_rate_limited (drive.py:906-923; the search at 912-919); round 3 left 'resets' out (its review 13, F6). tests/test_routing.py TestRound3Sources re-derives the tuple with ast from drive.py:149 and runs round 3's own matched_marker against routing's match. Plan: 'a pre-registered rate-limit marker in the API-error record'. Keys are API-error record fields (routing.py checks this).

operator_reasons_status: FILLED 6 Oct 2026 under Javier's ruling "gap4 routing: A" (typed 17:52:33 EDT in glitch-f3's window; plans/gap-study-round-4.md): round 3's 24 rehearsal_reasons, read with git show from evals/gap-study-3/prereg.json at e2979b3143081824aadea73523ec41af30c1ddb1 and checked equal to the ids evals/gap-study-3/check_take.py emits there, less the three the plan makes graded events (checker_reasons_become_events). Copied, not judged: each id routes by the plan's generic rule, a rehearsal before the agent's first turn and harness-error after it. tests/test_routing.py TestRound3Sources re-derives all of it.

no-first-agent-turn.meaning: the process exited, or the transcript holds no agent text, before the agent's first turn

readers-disagree.meaning: the transcript reader and the record reader count different numbers of user turns

unknown-harness-origin.meaning: a user record carries a harness origin this file does not name

no-session-id.meaning: the transcript records no session id

script-not-a-list.meaning: the half's operator script is not a list of turns

operator-lines.meaning: a scripted line was not sent, was sent twice or in the wrong order, a recovery exceeded its limit, or a line not on the script was sent

stop-at-held-marker.meaning: the driver stopped at a marker it read as unheld, and the agent's reply holds it

fixture-binding.meaning: the fixture the driver built is not the half's pinned fixture, or the record of it is unreadable

leak-in-operator-turn.meaning: an operator line contains a pre-registered leak word

leak-in-loaded-context.meaning: the session's loaded context contains a leak word outside a pinned excusal

inherited-context.meaning: the session was given an instruction file, a working directory or a connector tool from outside its checkout

project-name.meaning: no operator line names the neutral project name derived from the session id

session-binding.meaning: the transcript is not bound by its session id to a committed ledger row of this task and half

invocation.meaning: the checker was called with a ledger row for a walk, or without one for a take

model-binding.meaning: an assistant record carries a model other than the one the attempt is registered to

constant-binding.meaning: the take's ledger shows a turn budget or permission mode other than the pre-registered ones, or no ledger

continued-past-unheld-marker.meaning: an operator line was sent after a reply that did not hold the previous step's marker, or a recovery was sent where its own marker was not held

checkout-binding.meaning: the session's recorded git status or loaded instruction file is not the checkout the driver builds from the pinned tree

stop-without-a-wait-point.meaning: the ledger records a stop at a step that carries no wait point, or with a further operator line sent after it

outcome-binding.meaning: the ledger's outcome is not one the pinned driver writes, or a turn row carries no exit code, or the outcome disagrees with the driver's own record of the run: a completed take whose turn was cut or whose last reply stops short of the end of a turn, or a take published as cut with no cut behind it

environment-record.meaning: the attempt's environment record is absent or unreadable, or disagrees with the draft's vocabulary, its transcript's session, its row's commit, its ledger or its own turns

checker_reasons_become_events.source: Plan, CP2 check_take.py task: "The `study-materials-reached` and `account-email` reasons (check_take.py:1682, 714) become events, graded as usual with the text masked"; and "Outside reads (1687-1704) ... are recorded as events, not rehearsals" (read-outside-the-checkout, check_take.py:1691 at e2979b31). Round 4's checker emits them as events, so routing never sees them as reasons; an id here that still arrived as a reason would be refused, never defaulted.

pin_profiles_status: PENDING (CP5). One profile per model the round runs: the model id, and the permission mode and Claude Code version pre-registered for it. The init-mismatch row compares every init event with the take's pin, and routing.py refuses a pin that is not the pre-registered profile of its model, so the driver is never trusted for it. Until CP5 pre-registers the profiles, routing.py refuses every take and batch.py refuses to start.

rows.source: Plan table row 1: 'before the agent's first turn | preflight failure'. Also a box-only record (CP1 task: 'the box-only records (preflight, ...)').
Plan table row 1: 'container start failure'. Lane w1b decision: a container that started and exited before the first turn counts as a start failure.

Plan table row 1: 'API error'. A rate-limit marker also matches rate-limit (pause), which wins on precedence. Phase per the gap4 lane lead's ruling on W1B-5: the agent's first turn starts with the first turn that produced completed agent output (a text or tool-call message, read from the stream's event types), so an API error in a turn that produced none, however that turn ended (in error, or timed out), is before the agent's first turn. Review round 2 (W1B2-1) reverted 3fcab58d, which had let any timed-out turn start the agent's turn and so sent this row's silent-timeout cases to harness-error; glitch-f3's correction (6 Oct 2026; glitch-f3's, not the owner's) keeps a silent timeout before the first turn (see silent-timeout-before-first-turn).

CP1 task: 'the box-only records (preflight, sidecar health, ...)'. Lane w1b decision: a watcher fault before the first turn is a rehearsal, as every other harness fault in that phase. The stop record is not read here: before the first turn it may legitimately not exist yet.
Plan table last row: 'each operator-side reason the copied checker keeps ... a rehearsal before the first turn'. Matches any id in operator_reasons (PENDING, see operator_reasons_status).

CP1 task: 'The sidecar's health and the operator-diff check run inside that same step'; CP3 endstate: 'The drive step has already routed any operator-step diff that no event explains'. Phase split as the plan's last row.
Plan table last row: 'round 3's finalize abort (drive.py:1417) ... a rehearsal before the first turn'. Cited from the plan text; evals/gap-study-3/drive.py was not read by lane w1b.

glitch-f3's correction (6 Oct 2026, relayed by the gap4 lane lead; recorded as glitch-f3's, not the owner's), which withdrew his earlier acceptance that a timed-out silent first turn is the agent's: "A silent timeout with no completed agent output can't be told apart from a hung API, CLI or egress using harness records, and round 3 already routes it as rehearsal through no-first-agent-turn. 'A timeout stays the agent's' applies once the agent has produced completed output." Plan table row 1: before the agent's first turn, a harness fault is a rehearsal. This row's route is its one value in routing.json: a ruling change is a one-word edit of it. It sits at rehearsal's level, so every before-first-turn harness row it meets (an API error, an operator reason such as no-first-agent-turn, a container exit, a preflight failure) names the same route and is one answer with it, and the rate-limit row (pause) outranks it. Review round 2, W1B2-1 (the gap4 lane lead's brief): its own row, any_of ledger.end eq timed-out, none_of an init event that differs from the pin, so a silent timeout under the wrong model, mode or version (or with no init event) matches no row and is refused for a human.

Plan table: 'any time | a pre-registered rate-limit marker in the API-error record | pause'. Every API error of the take is read (W1B-4): a marker on any one of them matches. A marker in any of the record's three fields matches: structured status or type, OR round 3's text markers in the harness-side error text, never the agent's (glitch-f3's ruling, 6 Oct 2026; see rate_limit_markers.source).
Plan table: 'after the first turn | the turn's out-of-memory or pids-limit counters rose ... whatever the exit looked like | aborted ... never re-run'.
Plan table: 'after the first turn | API-error record'.
Plan table: 'after the first turn | ... container exit'.
Plan table: 'a watcher gap (start or stop record missing, non-zero exit, queue overflow)'; edge case: 'The watcher overflows or dies mid-take: the take routes as harness-error'.

Plan table: 'an init event whose model, mode or version differs from the pin'; testing strategy: 'a mismatch on the last turn of an otherwise graded take is a harness-error'. Lane w1b decision: a turn with no init event at all counts as a mismatch.

Plan table: 'after the first turn | a non-zero exec exit with no API-error record and no rise in those counters | harness-error'. Lane w1b decision: the exit of a turn the host ended as timed-out is not read, because 'a timeout stays the agent's' and the host's own kill exits non-zero.
Plan table last row: '... harness-error after it'. Matches any id in operator_reasons (PENDING, see operator_reasons_status).
CP3 endstate VALIDATE: 'an unexplained diff that routes as harness-error'.
Plan table last row: round 3's finalize abort (drive.py:1417), 'harness-error after it'.

annotations_about: Annotations are decided on every take, in every phase, whatever route wins and even when routing refuses the take: they never route. An annotation holds when at least one of its any_of conditions holds; it is reported as an event when event is true, and sets mask (the take's text is masked, never deleted, before commit) when mask is true.

annotations.source: Plan table: 'any time | the agent's own text or actions reaching the token, the account email, a study path or anything outside the run tree | graded as usual; the text is masked, never deleted, before commit, and counted as an event'. Read from the drive step's count, never from the text. Review round 1 (W1B-1): an annotation on every take in every phase, independent of the routing rows and of how the last turn ended, so it never routes and is never lost.

CP1 task: 'the box-only records (..., a quiescence kill)'; CP3 endstate: 'Writes by a background process the driver recorded and stopped at the cap are attributed to the turn that launched it'. Lane w1b decision: the agent's own behaviour, counted as an event; it does not route (the take routes by its other records, graded on a graded end). Review round 1 (W1B-1): an annotation, on every take.

Review round 2 (W1B2-2). Plan, CP2 check_take.py task: the study-materials-reached and account-email reasons 'become events, graded as usual with the text masked', and outside reads 'are recorded as events, not rehearsals' (checker_reasons_become_events). Round 4's checker emits them as events, which the drive step counts in events.outside_reach. If one still arrives as a checker reason, routing refuses the take (the id is not an operator reason, and never may be: routing.py checks the two lists are disjoint), so batch.py commits it blocked; this annotation holds on every take whose checker_reasons carry any of those ids, whatever route wins or whether one does, so the event is still counted and the text masked, never lost to the refusal.
